question.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta +2\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(r) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\,(\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta +2\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }\,(\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta +2\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot ({sec}^{2}⁡\theta -2{csc}^{2}⁡\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}=-\frac{1}{3}$ and $\theta =\frac{2\pi }{3},$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot [{sec}^{2}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})-2{csc}^{2}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})] \\ -\frac{1}{3} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot (4-\frac{8}{3}) \\ -\frac{1}{3} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{4}{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} & =-\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
